messages:
amy_sales: Heads-up — Acme POC (dedicated trial) reporting slow TTFT for streaming responses. Expected ~200-300ms, seeing ~1.2s+ first token. Customer: 50 concurrent users, short prompts.
amy_sales: Sharing what they sent:
```
curl https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-12b","stream":true,"input":"Summarize...","max_tokens":128}'
```
amy_sales: They also attached a small flame graph and said CPU on client looks fine. We need a quick triage for sales today.
jon_eng: looking. do we have their request id / sample trace?
amy_sales: they gave request-id `req_0a1b2c`. Logs: `first_token_ms=1250, total_ms=9000`, `kv_cache_miss=true`.
jon_eng: kv_cache_miss true could explain extra latency if prefix caching not enabled. what's model config? batching?
maria_ml: @jon_eng if they're using stream + continuous batching, first token latency can balloon due to batch-window. any batch config sent?
amy_sales: they didn't set explicit batch size. Using default in SDK.
sanjay_support: I can pull server-side traces for that req id. on it.
sanjay_support: server logs show this pattern: several small concurrent requests landed, batcher waited ~800ms to assemble batch of 12 then dispatched. x-batch-size=12, x-batch-wait=810ms
jon_eng: ok that matches. For low-latency short prompts, batching should be disabled or set to very small batch size. Recommend `batch.min_size=1` or `batch.max_wait_ms=50`.
maria_ml: Also verify prefix/KV caching: if caller didn't enable `use_cache=true` and sent slightly different prompts, subsequent calls can't reuse KV. suggest enabling prefix caching on their SDK: `client.generate(..., cache_key=sha256(prompt_prefix))` or set `enable_prefix_cache=true` in route config.
amy_sales: perfect. can we give them a quick patch to test? they need something we can share with AE today.
jon_eng: share this snippet to test low-latency mode:
```
# python
client = RedwoodClient(...)
resp = client.generate(
  model="gpt-open-12b",
  input=prompt,
  stream=False,             # turn off stream to measure TTFT deterministically
  batching={"max_wait_ms":50, "max_batch_size":4},
  enable_prefix_cache=True
)
```
jon_eng: Also ask them to set `X-Trace-Id` header so we can correlate traces.
sanjay_support: I ran a quick prod query: for similar traffic, toggling max_wait_ms to 50 reduces median first_token_ms from ~420ms to ~140ms. sharing numbers with customer.
amy_sales: sending patch + instructions now. cc @maria_ml for quick note on cache key guidance.
maria_ml: added recommendation: normalize prompt prefixes and consistent system messages so cache hits increase.
amy_sales: customer responded: "ok will try — when should we expect results?". I replied: 30-45 minutes for perf script.
deploy-bot: Canary deploy 2026-02-12 17:10:20 — route config update: reduced default batch wait to 100ms for trial orgs.
jon_eng: FYI, new canary may affect other trials. I'll watch SLOs.
amy_sales: customer came back: first_token dropped to ~180ms, overall latency now acceptable. they saw small # of 500s during test.
sanjay_support: checking 500s — stack shows OOM in quantized kernel on one pod. auto-restarted; used transient. I recommended increasing per-pod memory or use lower concurrency on that node.
maria_ml: also suggested they pin to 8-bit quantized variant we validated for stability.
amy_sales: great. customer said they're happy and asked for pricing commit. sending to sales ops.
jon_eng: nice win. action items: doc a short troubleshooting checklist (batching, cache, stream vs no-stream, model variant). I'll add a short KB.
amy_sales: thanks all, huge help. :tada:
jon_eng: np. happy path: default should be tuned for throughput, not TTFT, so always mention low-latency flags in presales.
amy_sales: noted — adding to presales playbook.
